examples.en: I can hear the children singing in the classroom.
Cheerful singing can be heard from somewhere too.
I couldn't sleep because of the singing.
I woke up to the singing from next door.
That singer's voice is really clear.

examples.ko: 노랫소리를 따라가 보니 작은 공원이 나왔어요.
examples.en: I followed the sound of singing and came to a small park.

explain: '노래'와 '소리'가 합쳐지면서 사이시옷이 들어가서 '노래소리'가 아니라 '노랫소리'라고 써요. '목소리'는 사람의 목소리 자체이고, '노랫소리'는 노래하는 소리예요.
explain_en: When '노래' and '소리' join, a 사이시옷 is added, so write '노랫소리', not '노래소리'. '목소리' is a person's voice itself, while '노랫소리' is the sound of singing.

examples.ko: 우리 반 친구가 수업 시간에 자주 농담해요.
examples.en: A classmate of mine often jokes during class.
My uncle joked with a smile at the dinner table.
Don't joke with me like that.
They're someone who likes to joke.
If you joke sometimes, the mood gets better.

examples.ko: 기분 나쁘게 하려고 농담한 게 아니에요.
examples.en: I didn't joke to upset you.

explain: '농담하다'보다 '농담을 하다'라고 더 자주 말해요. 반대말은 '진담'이라서 '농담이에요', '농담이죠?'처럼 짧게도 많이 써요. 윗사람에게는 '농담하지 마세요'가 강하게 들릴 수 있으니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 농담 반 진담 반으로 한 말인데 친구가 진지하게 받아들였어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃으며 말했지만 속마음도 조금 섞여 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you said something with a smile but part of it was meant seriously.

explain_en: People say '농담을 하다' more often than '농담하다'. The opposite is '진담' (serious talk), and short lines like '농담이에요' and '농담이죠?' are very common. '농담하지 마세요' can sound harsh to someone older, so be careful.

examples.en: My shoulders hurt, so I got a massage.
Sitting in a massage chair relieves my tiredness.
The massage felt so good that I got sleepy.
This hotel also has a massage service.
I showed my thanks to my grandmother with a massage.
Drink plenty of water after a massage.

explain: '안마 의자', '안마기'처럼 쓰는 말이고, 가게에서는 '마사지'라는 말도 같이 써요. 가족의 어깨를 풀어 드릴 때는 '주물러 드리다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It appears in words like 안마 의자 and 안마기, and shops also use the word 마사지. When you rub a family member's shoulders, you can also say 주물러 드리다.

examples.en: My child loves jelly so much.
Jelly is soft and very sweet.
I bought a fruit jelly at the convenience store.

examples.ko: 젤리를 많이 먹으면 이가 아플 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat a lot of jelly, your teeth may hurt.
I brought jelly when I went to the movie theater.
I gave my friend some bear-shaped jelly.

explain: 한국에서 '젤리'는 과일즙으로 굳힌 디저트보다 말랑하고 쫀득한 과자를 먼저 떠올리는 경우가 많아요. 편의점에는 곰 모양, 과일 모양 젤리가 많아요. 우유와 달걀로 만든 부드러운 '푸딩'과는 달라요.
explain_en: In Korea, '젤리' often brings to mind a soft, chewy candy first rather than a fruit-juice dessert. Convenience stores sell many bear-shaped and fruit-shaped jellies. It differs from '푸딩', a soft dessert made with milk and eggs.

examples.en: I'm talking on the phone with my friend at the office now.
I talked with my mother on the phone for an hour yesterday.
I'd like to talk on the phone for a moment; is now okay?
I'm on a call right now, so I'll phone you later.
I'm too busy today, so it's hard to talk on the phone.

examples.ko: 회의 때문에 오래 통화할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't talk on the phone for long because of the meeting.

explain: '전화하다'는 전화를 거는 행동이고, '통화하다'는 연결돼서 서로 말하는 데 초점이 있어요. 그래서 '통화 중이에요', '통화가 안 돼요'처럼 연결 상태를 말할 때도 많이 써요. 보통 '친구와 통화하다'처럼 '와/과'랑 같이 써요.
explain_en: '전화하다' is the act of making a call, while '통화하다' focuses on being connected and actually talking. That is why you also hear '통화 중이에요' (the line is busy) and '통화가 안 돼요' (I can't get through). It usually goes with '와/과', as in '친구와 통화하다'.

examples.en: I often listen to pop music.
I heard a pop singer is coming to Korea.
This song mixes pop and K-pop.
Many of my friends study English through pop songs.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 팝을 들으면서 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I danced while listening to pop.
Do you like music other than pop too?

explain: '팝'은 혼자보다 '팝 음악', '팝 가수'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙을 때가 많아요. '팝송'은 보통 영어 노래를 가리키고, 한국 노래는 '가요'나 'K팝'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 팝 usually appears with another word, as in 팝 음악 and 팝 가수. 팝송 normally means English-language songs, while Korean songs are called 가요 or K팝.
